overall_summary: Bitcoin is under pressure from escalating US-Iran tensions closing the Strait of Hormuz, driving oil higher and stoking inflation fears that are pushing yields and the dollar up. Positive crypto news like strong ETF inflows and Circle's bank approval offer some support, but geopolitical risks dominate the near-term tone. Markets now brace for tomorrow's CPI data amid the uncertainty.
key_points: Iran tensions close Hormuz, oil surges
Circle wins OCC national trust approval
BTC slips under $63K on geo risks

items.title: BTC slips under $63K on Iran tensions, Asia leverage flush
items.summary: Bitcoin fell about 1.5 to 2 percent to around $62,800 after sliding from over $64,000 in the Asian session. Reignited US-Iran hostilities over the Strait of Hormuz pressured risk assets, while about $253 million in liquidations hit, mostly longs, though volumes were relatively modest. The drop stays inside Bitcoin's recent $59,000 to $66,000 range. Traders should watch for further risk-off spillover or a clean flush setting up a bounce, with CPI data due soon.
items.impact: Short-term pressure but range-bound with limited liquidations

items.title: Spot BTC ETFs post $197M weekly inflows, end outflow streak
items.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded roughly $197 million in net inflows for the week ending July 10, snapping an eight-to-nine week streak of outflows that had totaled several billion dollars. BlackRock's IBIT led the inflows. This institutional buying occurred even as price dipped on geopolitics. It signals potential returning demand that can help stabilize or support prices going forward.
items.impact: Positive institutional demand supporting price floors

items.title: Strategy holds 843,775 BTC steady, raises $467M via shares
items.summary: Strategy's latest 8-K shows no Bitcoin purchases or sales in the week ended July 12, with holdings unchanged at 843,775 BTC valued around $63.7 billion. The company sold 4.82 million shares under its ATM program for $466.7 million net proceeds and reported USD reserves at $3 billion. No share repurchases occurred. This keeps supply pressure off Bitcoin while bolstering the company's cash position.
items.impact: No new corporate buying or selling pressure on BTC

items.title: BIP-110 data-limit softfork nears deadline with zero miner support
items.summary: The BIP-110 proposal for a temporary soft fork to limit arbitrary data on Bitcoin and curb spam or inscriptions is approaching key deadlines with miner signaling near zero. Michael Saylor and others have publicly criticized it as risky or misguided. The community remains split between protecting Bitcoin as money versus risks of chain splits or reduced flexibility. Unresolved protocol debates like this can inject uncertainty into markets.
items.impact: Potential short-term noise from community division

items.title: Circle wins final OCC approval for national trust bank
items.summary: Circle, the issuer of USDC, received final approval from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency to establish a national trust bank called Circle National Trust. This puts digital asset custody under direct federal banking oversight and paves the way for potential future management of USDC reserves. The news boosted Circle shares and marks a key step in integrating stablecoins into the regulated banking system. Traders care because stronger USDC infrastructure supports overall market liquidity and institutional confidence.
items.impact: Boosts stablecoin trust and regulated crypto adoption

items.title: Resurgent Iran hostilities weigh on BTC despite ETF demand
items.summary: Fresh US-Iran airstrikes and statements that the ceasefire is over pressured Bitcoin lower even as spot ETF flows indicated ongoing demand. Oil rose while risk assets including crypto saw selling. Bitcoin has shown relative resilience compared to some traditional markets in recent geo flares. Watch for escalation near the Strait of Hormuz as a volatility driver alongside upcoming macro data.
items.impact: Geopolitical risk premium and volatility risk

items.title: Oil Surges as US-Iran Tensions Close Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: Renewed military exchanges between the US and Iran have led Tehran to close the Strait of Hormuz, sending oil prices up over 4 percent toward 80 dollars a barrel. European shares opened lower and global markets are pricing in higher energy costs. Crypto traders should watch this closely because elevated oil feeds directly into inflation prints and keeps the Fed on a hawkish path, which typically pressures risk assets like Bitcoin.
items.impact: Higher inflation risks and risk-off pressure on crypto and equities

items.title: Markets Brace for June CPI and Warsh Testimony Tomorrow
items.summary: June consumer price index data drops Tuesday morning, followed immediately by Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's first congressional testimony as chairman before the House. PPI and Senate testimony come Wednesday. Traders care because these will set the tone for the July FOMC meeting and rate-hike odds; a hot CPI print plus hawkish Warsh comments could lock in higher-for-longer rates.
items.impact: High volatility catalyst for rates, dollar, and risk assets this week

items.title: US 10-Year Yield Climbs Toward 4.6% on Oil Inflation Fears
items.summary: The benchmark 10-year Treasury yield rose to around 4.59 percent Monday as oil spiked on Middle East tensions. Bond markets are reassessing the persistence of inflation pressures. Higher real yields raise the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding assets like Bitcoin and can trigger risk-off flows across financial markets.
items.impact: Tighter financial conditions and headwind for Bitcoin and equities

items.title: Fed Monetary Policy Report Flags Elevated Inflation Drivers
items.summary: The Fed's latest report to Congress, still circulating into this week, said inflation stepped up further due to tariffs, the Iran war energy shock, and the AI buildout. PCE remains roughly double the 2 percent target. This reinforces market pricing of possible rate hikes later in 2026 and keeps dollar and yields supported until data proves otherwise.
items.impact: Supports higher rate path and pressure on crypto risk appetite

items.title: Dollar Index Holds Near 101 Amid Geopolitical Premium
items.summary: The US dollar index is trading around 100.9 to 101 as safe-haven and inflation-hedge demand lingers with Middle East risks. A firm dollar typically weighs on crypto prices in the short term by reducing global liquidity and making dollar-denominated assets more expensive for foreign buyers.
items.impact: Headwind for Bitcoin and risk assets via stronger greenback

items.title: Fed's Bowman Speaks on Regulatory Modernization Today
items.summary: Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman delivered remarks in London on modernizing financial regulation, focusing on risk-based supervision, capital reforms, and AI adoption. While not a direct rates speech, any comments on banking conditions or broader economy can move markets. Traders should listen for hints on the growth-inflation tradeoff under the new Fed leadership.
items.impact: Limited direct rates impact but monitors for policy tone shifts

items.title: US-Iran Strikes Escalate Over Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: The United States and Iran traded heavy missile and drone strikes over the weekend into Monday, with Iran targeting US facilities across Gulf states including Qatar, UAE, Bahrain, Kuwait and others, while declaring the Strait of Hormuz closed again. US Central Command hit dozens to hundreds of Iranian targets to degrade attacks on shipping after a container ship was struck. Brent crude jumped more than 4 percent to around 78 to 80 dollars a barrel as traffic through the vital oil chokepoint plummeted. Traders should care because this revives energy supply risks, fuels inflation worries and drives risk-off moves across markets including crypto.
items.impact: Higher oil prices and geopolitical risk premium pressure risk assets

items.title: UK Proscribes Iran's IRGC as Terrorist Group
items.summary: Britain has designated Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps as a terrorist organisation, Sky News and Reuters report, making membership or support a criminal offence. The IRGC was already under sanctions but this formal ban escalates pressure amid the ongoing US-Iran conflict. It signals deeper Western isolation of Tehran. Crypto traders should watch because it raises the chance of further Iranian retaliation or tighter energy disruptions.
items.impact: Heightens escalation risks and potential sanctions/oil volatility

items.title: Zelenskyy Replaces Ukraine Prime Minister
items.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy announced he will replace Prime Minister Yulia Svyrydenko after only a year, triggering a full government resignation for an updated political strategy. The move comes amid major corruption scandals involving figures close to the president, including at the state nuclear company. Lawmakers say possible successors include energy or defence figures. This matters for traders as it signals internal instability that could affect Western support and the war's trajectory.
items.impact: Political uncertainty in Ukraine may weigh on European risk sentiment

items.title: Senator Lindsey Graham Dies at 71
items.summary: US Republican Senator Lindsey Graham of South Carolina, a key Trump ally and defence hawk who strongly backed Ukraine and Israel while opposing Iran, has died after a brief sudden illness. Trump called him a hard-working patriot; Zelenskyy and Netanyahu also paid tribute. His death creates a temporary Senate vacancy in a closely divided chamber that the governor can fill. Markets may note the loss of a reliable vote for Trump's agenda and pro-Ukraine policies.
items.impact: Minor near-term Senate dynamics shift with little immediate market effect

items.title: Nations Reject China's South China Sea Claims
items.summary: Japan, the Philippines, the United States and eleven other countries issued a joint statement on the 10th anniversary of the 2016 arbitral ruling, reaffirming that China's expansive maritime claims have no legal basis and the award is final and binding. China rejected it as waste paper, summoned Japan's envoy and blamed outside powers for tensions. This underscores ongoing Indo-Pacific frictions. Traders should note it as a background risk for trade routes and China-related assets.
items.impact: Sustains China-West tensions without immediate market catalyst

items.title: Germany Funds 50,000 Attack Drones for Ukraine
items.summary: Germany is financing a roughly 90 million euro order of 50,000 Shrike FPV strike drones made by Ukrainian firm SkyFall with Auterion software, one of the largest such Western packages. Some have already been delivered, with more due this year. Ukraine produces millions of drones annually and relies on them heavily. This bolsters Kyiv's capabilities amid the grinding war and shows continued European military support.
items.impact: Supports Ukraine war effort without major near-term market shift
